title: Bar Chatiya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Bereshit Rabbah 30:8: “Everyone of whom ‘blameless’ is said had his years divided into thirds according to the measure of a week.” He says this SHOULD ALSO BE THE READING in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 105a. Hyman cites Midrash Mishlei 22:2 for Bar Chuniya and says it SHOULD READ Chatiya. Bereshit Rabbah 53:12 has R’ Azaryah in the name of Bar Chatiya; Shir HaShirim Rabbah, at the supplied 5:4, has Bar Chuta saying: “Why is it called Alef? Because it agrees from a thousand generations” [the explanation remains uncertain].
It appears to Hyman that his name was Shimon, as in Bereshit Rabbah 26:3.

notes.text: The supplied Hebrew says השליש (“divided into thirds”); the checked Bereshit Rabbah 30:8 says השלים (“completed his years to a measure of seven”). That difference remains unresolved. The second Alef/thousand-generations saying is also obscure; the requested Shir HaShirim Rabbah text was unavailable.

The saved whole Torat Emet Shir Ha Shirim Rabbah 5:11:4 scalar contains Bar Chuta’s Alef/thousand-generations saying in its letter discussion, beside supplied 5:4. This supersedes the old blanket unavailable-text statement without proving a printed locator error. מסכים מאלף דור remains lexically uncertain. The earlier Bereshit Rabbah comparison has השלים, completed, versus supplied השליש, divided into thirds; no fresh Bereshit scalar was inspected. Pesikta 105a is edition-dependent. Hyman’s SHOULD READ Chatiya and his possible Shimon identification retain their force and uncertainty. No full title is transferred to the uninspected Azaryah occurrence.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 286) reads השליש, which the translation renders “divided into thirds.” The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 30:8 and Yalkut on Psalms 730:3 read השלים, completing the years to a multiple of seven. Buber’s Pesikta 105a gives Ben Chuniya in the passage on Proverbs 22:20. Its note cites Ben Chuta and the Yalkut’s Bar Chatiya. The consulted digital Pesikta 12:5 instead has Bar Chuta. Buber’s Midrash Mishlei gives Bar Chuniya in the corresponding passage, and the Yalkut on Proverbs 960 gives Bar Chatiya. Hyman’s proposed corrected readings and possible identification as Shimon remain his.
